chunks: About a marked garment: may a man enter ihram in it? He said, "Yes. Only the mulham garment is disliked."

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: garment or clothing being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man subject to the legal ruling
key_terms.الْمُعْلَمِ: marked or patterned in a limited way
key_terms.الْمُلْحَمُ: a fully patterned or heavily decorated garment
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: is disliked, though not necessarily forbidden

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to enter ihram wearing a marked garment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about clothing worn in the state of ihram. It indicates that entering ihram in a marked garment is permissible, while what is considered disliked is the mulham garment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2606 - Laith al-Muradi asked Imam (as) about a man entering Ihram in an embroidered garment.
Imam (as) said: "Yes, it is permissible. What is disliked is a fully patterned garment (mulham)."
